Source comparison: a star has different limiting exponents while a clique has Lambert-W rather than golden-ratio scaling.
value.rationale: Complete bipartite graphs are a natural two-community transport family. The entropy rate measures unpredictability of actual observed trajectories. The theorem gives an actionable root-side preference for every finite part imbalance, together with a nontrivial all-optimizer asymptotic and exact golden-ratio intensity in dense balanced networks. These results identify a structural transition from previously studied star and clique reset scales and cannot be inferred from generic entropy positivity or routine parameter renaming; no sweeping practical impact is asserted.
residual_risks: Empirical network applications with hidden reset labels, weighted walks, or other objectives are not covered.
